trajectory_summary: This is a short, mechanically-run verify call where the rep moves through script items quickly but leaves at least two data points — the co-owner question and the exact bill amount — unresolved and un-clarified. The customer stayed cooperative throughout, including surfacing a spontaneous Tesla question, but the rep's pace didn't create space to nail down ambiguous answers, and the call ends on a text-and-callback plan with no locked appointment.
outcome_dispute: This call did not produce a booked or tentative appointment — it ended with the rep promising to text the customer and call back once she sends a bill photo. It should be tagged callback, not booked or tentative, since no day or time was set.

observed_outcome.quote: When you get home, you can just take a picture of that graph, send it to me, and then I'll call you, and then we'll schedule you. Okay?
observed_outcome.reasoning: No day or time was set on this call; the rep explicitly frames the next step as a future call once the bill photo is received, which is a callback with no locked time, not a booked or tentative appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The customer's bill answer came through garbled and self-corrected three times in a row without the rep ever clarifying or confirming the actual figure, and the rep responded only with 'Okay' before moving straight to the roof question — no emotional flip or even a confirmed number was executed.

bill_document_audit.result_quote: When you get home, you can just take a picture of that graph, send it to me
bill_document_audit.reasoning: The customer could not access the bill online or in person while at work, so the rep pivoted to having her text a photo of the usage graph once home, deferring bill collection to after the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked what interested the customer in solar; the call moved straight from intro into address/homeowner/utility verify questions without this qualifier ever being raised.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: unanchored soft exit / no locked callback time
primary_coaching_focus.quote: When you get home, you can just take a picture of that graph, send it to me, and then I'll call you, and then we'll schedule you. Okay?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The call ends with a vague plan and zero locked commitment — no callback time, no day/time for the appointment. This is the single biggest fixable gap: a specific callback window costs nothing and materially improves the odds this lead doesn't go cold.

key_moments.quote: Okay. So it's a single family home. Is there anybody else I'm entitled but you?
key_moments.stewart_read: The co-owner question was asked but the exchange that followed (00:28-00:36) is garbled and inconclusive, and the rep never circled back to confirm who else is on title. This is a critical unresolved gap for closer handoff since spouse/co-owner presence at the appointment is a booking-fragility factor.

The bill figure comes through garbled and self-corrected three times ($2.80 → $3.80 → 300) and the rep never clarifies which number is accurate or whether it's dollars or hundreds. The rep says only 'Okay' and moves straight to the roof question.

Strategy match failure: the bill was captured (in some garbled form) but never flipped into any framing about the customer's expense or paired with a follow-up question — the rep simply logs it and asks about the roof next.

key_moments.quote: Oh, are you able to ask? About Tesla, solar. Right?
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer volunteers an unprompted question about the Tesla partnership — a spontaneous engagement signal the rep could have used to build rapport or curiosity about the appointment.
